title: The Great Roll and the Witnesses
summary: Nephi reports the Lord’s instruction concerning a great roll and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. He then reports taking unto himself faithful witnesses, Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

explicit_facts.text: The word of the Lord instructs Nephi to take a great roll and write in it with a man’s pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

Nephi reports taking unto himself faithful witnesses: Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah. The text includes the phrase “to record,” but does not describe any recording being performed.

unspecified_visual_details: The location and the characters’ appearances are unspecified.
The roll’s material and dimensions and the pen’s appearance are unspecified.
How the word of the Lord was conveyed is unspecified.
The interval between the instruction and the taking of witnesses is unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man’s pen, concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: Moreover, the word of the Lord said unto me:
And I took unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the first-person narrator.
The dialogue is the Lord’s reported instruction, not a newly enacted speaking event or evidence of a visible divine appearance.
Keep both verses as a narrated report; do not stage the reported events as new present-tense action or merge their times.
The text does not specify what the witnesses record or narrate their performing that action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent a means of communication.
Do not depict the commanded writing as underway or completed.
Do not stage the taking of witnesses or recording as present-tense action.
Do not place Uriah or Zechariah at the instruction.
Do not depict Maher-shalal-hash-baz or Jeberechiah as present.
Do not identify Maher-shalal-hash-baz as a child or Nephi’s son.
Do not assert that the witnesses record writing on the roll.

title: The Child Is Named
summary: Nephi reports going to the prophetess, who conceived and bore a son. The Lord then tells him to name the child Maher-shalal-hash-baz and predicts that Damascus’s riches and Samaria’s spoil will be taken before the child knows how to cry for his father and mother.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi reports going to the prophetess, who conceived and bore a son.
The Lord tells Nephi to name the child Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
The Lord predicts that the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be taken before the king of Assyria before the child knows how to cry for his father and mother.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown listening during the Lord’s instruction, without depicting the Lord.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance and clothing
The setting of the naming instruction
Whether the prophetess and child are present during the instruction

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, the child shall not have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, before the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived and bare a son.
Then said the Lord to me:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Present the reported visit, conception, and birth in narration before the Lord’s naming instruction.
The taking of riches and spoil is a prediction, not an event occurring in this scene.
My father, and my mother is part of the Lord’s prediction, not speech by the child.
prohibited_inventions: Do not visibly depict the Lord; no appearance is described.
Do not dramatize the reported visit, conception, or birth as present-tense action.
Do not depict the predicted taking of riches and spoil.
Do not invent additional dialogue, the prophetess’s name, or a parental relationship for Nephi.
Do not place the king of Assyria physically in the scene.

title: The Lord Speaks Again
summary: The Lord speaks again to Nephi, saying that this people refuse the softly flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord speaks again to the first-person narrator.
The Lord says that this people refuse the waters of Shiloah that go softly and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and Nephi’s physical appearance are unspecified.
No visible appearance of the Lord is described.
The people, Shiloah, Rezin, and Remaliah’s son are not established as visible during the speech.

spoken_dialogue.text: Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: The Lord spake also unto me again, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people’s refusal and rejoicing are reported in the Lord’s speech, not staged as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible appearance of the Lord.
Do not stage the people’s refusal or rejoicing as a contemporaneous event.
Do not place Rezin or Remaliah’s son physically in the exchange.
Do not turn the waters into a supernatural spectacle or invent their interpretation.

title: Prophecy Concerning Assyria and Judah
summary: The passage foretells the king of Assyria's advance through Judah using river, overflow, and wings imagery.

explicit_facts.text: The prophecy says the Lord will bring up the waters of the river upon them and identifies this imagery with the king of Assyria and all his glory.
The prophecy says he will pass through Judah and uses overflow, neck, and wings imagery to describe the extent of his advance.
The prophecy addresses Immanuel but does not describe him as present.

unspecified_visual_details: No present setting or visible participants are specified.
The king's appearance and Judah's physical features are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified prophetic speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified prophetic speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified prophetic speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses give a prophecy, not an account of an advance occurring in the present scene.
The river, overflow, neck, and wings are prophetic imagery; the verses do not establish a literal flood or visible wings.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the foretold advance as a present event.
Do not depict the Lord or Immanuel as visibly present.
Do not invent a speaker, a physical setting, or appearances for the figures mentioned.

title: Counsel That Will Not Stand
summary: An unidentified speaker addresses people and those of far countries, warning that they will be broken in pieces and that their counsel and word will not stand.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker addresses people and those of far countries, calling on them to associate, give ear, and gird themselves.
The speaker repeatedly warns that they will be broken in pieces.
The speaker says their counsel will come to naught and their word will not stand, for God is with us.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speech can be presented without depicting the people addressed or the predicted outcomes.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance
The appearance of the people addressed

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: Take counsel together, and it shall come to naught; speak the word, and it shall not stand; for God is with us.

title: Do Not Fear Their Fear
summary: The Lord instructs the speaker not to follow the people's way and tells him not to fear their fear, but to sanctify the Lord of Hosts.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord speaks with a strong hand and instructs the speaker not to walk in the people's way.
The Lord tells the speaker not to say “A confederacy” as the people do, or to fear their fear.
The Lord says to sanctify the Lord of Hosts and let him be their fear and dread.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord's instruction may be conveyed as off-screen speech to the speaker.
unspecified_visual_details: The meaning or visual form of “with a strong hand”; the setting and the speaker's appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Sanctify the Lord of Hosts himself,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Strong hand” is not a described visible appearance of the Lord.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord physically or invent a visible hand.

title: Sanctuary and Stumbling Stone
summary: The Lord says he will be a sanctuary, yet also a stone of stumbling and a snare; many will stumble, fall, and be taken.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord shall be a sanctuary and also a stone of stumbling and rock of offense to both houses of Israel, and a snare to Jerusalem's inhabitants.
Many among them shall stumble, fall, be broken, be snared, and be taken.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The stone, rock, and snare can be represented metaphorically rather than as literal supernatural objects.
unspecified_visual_details: The people referred to and their appearance; the visual form of the metaphors.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The stone, rock, and snare are figures of speech, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal supernatural stone, rock, or trap.

title: Bind Up the Testimony
summary: An instruction calls for the testimony to be bound up and the law sealed among the speaker's disciples. Nephi says he will wait upon the Lord and look for him.

explicit_facts.text: The instruction says to bind up the testimony and seal the law among the speaker's disciples.
Nephi says he will wait upon the Lord and look for him.
Nephi describes the Lord as hiding his face from the house of Jacob.

summary: Nephi identifies himself and the children the Lord has given him as signs and wonders in Israel from the Lord of Hosts, who dwells in Mount Zion.
characters: The children given to Nephi by the Lord

explicit_facts.text: The Lord has given Nephi children.
Nephi and the children are for signs and wonders in Israel from the Lord of Hosts.
The Lord of Hosts dwells in Mount Zion.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and the children may be shown together, but the verse does not describe a particular gathering.
unspecified_visual_details: The children's number, ages, names, and appearance.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

title: To the Law and the Testimony
summary: The passage anticipates advice to seek those with familiar spirits and wizards, asks whether a people should seek their God, and directs attention to the law and testimony.

explicit_facts.text: The passage anticipates that unspecified people will advise others to seek those with familiar spirits and wizards who peep and mutter.
It asks whether a people should seek their God for the living to hear from the dead.
It invokes the law and the testimony and says that those who do not speak according to this word have no light in them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Display the warning as text rather than staging the anticipated advice as an event.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the identities and appearances of those addressed, and any visual design for the displayed text.

narration.text: And when they shall say unto you: Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep and mutter—should not a people seek unto their God for the living to hear from the dead?
To the law and to the testimony; and if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The advice is anticipated, not narrated as occurring. Hearing from the dead appears in a question, not as a narrated encounter. The verses do not identify a speaker for these statements.
prohibited_inventions: Do not attribute these statements to the Lord.
Do not depict spirits, wizards, communication with the dead, or the anticipated advice as an event taking place.

title: Driven to Darkness
summary: The verses foretell people passing through hardship and hunger, fretting, cursing their king and God, looking upward and toward the earth, beholding trouble and darkness, and being driven to darkness.

explicit_facts.text: They shall pass through hardship and hunger, fret, curse their king and their God, and look upward.
They shall look toward the earth, behold trouble, darkness, and dimness of anguish, and be driven to darkness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A prophetic illustration could show unidentified people looking upward and toward the earth, without presenting the prediction as a current event.
